audience: Content marketers, SEO practitioners, agencies, and small business site owners publishing AI-assisted content who want to know if they are at risk of a Google penalty

questions.question: Does Google penalize content simply for being AI-generated?
questions.answer_summary: No — Google's official guidance says it focuses on content quality and helpfulness, not on the production method; AI use alone is not a violation.

questions.question: What counts as 'scaled content abuse'?
questions.answer_summary: Producing many pages primarily to manipulate rankings, regardless of whether the content is AI-generated, human-written, or scraped — intent and lack of user value are what matter.

questions.question: Is using AI to help write blog posts against Google's guidelines?
questions.answer_summary: Not inherently — it becomes a violation only when AI/automation is used to mass-produce pages that don't add value for users.

questions.question: Should I disclose that content on my site was AI-generated?
questions.answer_summary: Google suggests providing background information on how automation was used, in a way that makes sense for the audience, as a transparency practice rather than a hard requirement.

questions.question: Why did some sites get a manual action tied to AI content?
questions.answer_summary: Reported manual actions have targeted mass-produced, low-value pages (scaled content abuse) rather than AI use by itself.

questions.question: Does AI-written content actually rank worse than human-written content?
questions.answer_summary: Independent research cited found no link between AI use and lower rankings, with the large majority of top-ranking pages surveyed containing at least some AI-assisted content.

questions.question: What's the difference between using AI as a writing aid and 'scaled content abuse'?
questions.answer_summary: Human oversight, originality, and genuine added value are what separate acceptable AI-assisted content from abuse, per Google's spam policy wording.

questions.question: Are AI-generated product descriptions okay for ecommerce SEO?
questions.answer_summary: Allowed if they add value; Google's ecommerce-related guidance recommends labeling AI-generated product images/media with IPTC DigitalSourceType metadata.

questions.question: Does 'spinning' or AI-rewriting scraped content count as spam?
questions.answer_summary: Yes — Google explicitly calls out scraping plus automated transformations like synonymizing or translating as a scaled-content-abuse pattern.

questions.question: What was the March 2024 helpful content update's connection to AI spam?
questions.answer_summary: It folded 'scaled content abuse' into Google's core spam policies, explicitly closing the loophole that had allowed mass-produced auto-generated content to rank.

questions.question: Is machine-generated traffic the same policy as AI-written content?
questions.answer_summary: No — these are separate spam policies (scaled content abuse for AI-written pages vs. machine-generated traffic for automated querying of Google), both filed under the broader 'automation' spam category.

questions.question: Can Google actually detect AI-written text?
questions.answer_summary: Google frames this as beside the point — its stated approach evaluates helpfulness/quality signals rather than trying to flag text as AI- vs. human-authored.
